`e2e/specs/56-list-grid.e2e.ts` has an intermittent failure on CI (desktop, `decorations` group).

The case is `puts space-indented levels on the grid whatever the space count` (around line 513). The failing assertion is:

    expect(row.markerX).toBeCloseTo(row.column, 1);

Observed on GitHub Actions run 34001303005 (job `desktop (decorations)`, commit 893c4c5 of branch `feat/backlinks-controls`): `Expected: 0, Received: 14.88`. So the row's marker sat roughly one marker-gutter to the right of the depth-0 column instead of on it.

Context that narrows it:
- The whole `decorations` group passes locally on macOS (8/8 spec files, 30 cases in 56-list-grid) at that same commit.
- It also passed on CI on the immediately preceding runs of the same branch, so it is not a new persistent break.
- The branch's only stylesheet changes at that point were all scoped under `.to-backlinks*` (the backlinks footer's own controls), so they cannot reach `.cm-line` list-grid decorations. The failure is very unlikely to be caused by that branch.

The case loops over three indent styles (`'  '`, `'   '`, `'\t'`) and rebuilds the note each time, so the first thing worth establishing is which iteration failed and whether the measurement ran before the layout settled — 14.88 is suspiciously close to one gutter, which suggests the marker was measured while the row was still being decorated, or that Obsidian's own indent rendering had not yet resolved.

Goal: reproduce it (running the group repeatedly, or under load / with more parallel instances, is the likely route since CI is slower than a dev machine), find the actual cause, and fix either the timing of the measurement or the underlying decoration if it is real. Read `docs/research/` notes on decorations and the list grid before changing anything — several mechanisms there were chosen by measurement and the comments record why.
I'll start by getting oriented — the spec, the research notes, and how the measurement is taken.

   * setting it on `body` moves the whole grid and nothing is left behind. That
   * only holds while nothing restates the value — no rule's `var()` fallback,
   * and nothing in JS (see `UNIT_EXPR`). */

  --to-guide-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--text-faint) 60%, transparent);
  --to-decor-accent: var(--text-accent);

   * colour: the line does not thicken as the caret moves into a subtree, and an
   * accented guide sits on exactly the columns and weight the unaccented one
   * did. A heavier value reads as emphasis-by-weight and makes the accented
   * column visibly jump; retune with a snippet if that is wanted. */

 * `--to-marker-gutter` (Experiment 5a, see
 * docs/research/10-experiment-5-block-markers.md): an additive reservation for
 * a per-kind block marker icon, on top of the existing depth-based
 * indentation. Its VALUE is derived from the marks it has to hold rather than
 * chosen (chrome-tokens.ts, docs/research/21-marker-text-gap.md), so no rule
 * here may restate it — a literal copy goes stale the first time that

 * `::after` with the guide or blockquote's native bar) a containing block
 * matching this line's own box.
 */
/* Two surfaces, one rule. The backlinks footer's rows are not `.cm-line`s and
 * are not children of `.cm-content`, but they carry the same class and the same
 * custom properties (`chrome-line.ts`), so they take the same layout from the
 * same declarations rather than from a parallel set that drifts. */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6 .cm-content > .cm-line.to-decor-block,
.to-backlinks-row.to-decor-block {

  padding-left: calc(
    var(--to-depth, 0) * var(--to-decor-unit) + var(--to-marker-gutter, 0px)
  ) !important;

   * enough to reclassify as an indented code block) get a native HyperMD
   * "hang" from Obsidian: a `padding-inline-start`/`text-indent` pair meant
   * to keep soft-wrapped continuation lines aligned under the first visible
   * character. Our own `padding-left` above always wins that fight (`!important`
   * beats a non-important inline style even across the logical/physical
   * property pair, confirmed live) — but `text-indent` is never touched by
   * us at all, so its native negative value (which Obsidian derives from a
   * measurement taken AFTER our own padding has already shifted the box,
   * confirmed live: for a single leading space the observed value wasn't
   * ~4px, the width of one space, but ~4px + our own padding-left, i.e. it
   * double-counts our own contribution) leaks straight through unopposed.
   * Net first-line shift becomes `ourPadding - nativeTextIndent`, which is
   * NEGATIVE — outdented past the depth column, growing with every extra
   * leading space (more native "measured" width to subtract), exactly the
   * reported bug. Zeroing text-indent removes the hang outright: the line
   * renders purely at our own depth position, and the literal leading
   * spaces still show up as ordinary rendered content on top of it (additive
   * -only, same invariant every other kind here already keeps) instead of
   * being folded into a hanging-indent calculation that assumes zero prior
   * padding. */

}

/* Atoms (code/table/quote/callout/html/hr) render a visible background or
 * border box; padding-left only shifts an element's own content, never
 * that box, so atoms need margin-left instead. */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6 .cm-content > .cm-line.to-decor-atom {
  position: relative;
  margin-left: calc(
    var(--to-depth, 0) * var(--to-decor-unit) + var(--to-marker-gutter, 0px)
  ) !important;
}

/* List items: the SUPPLEMENTAL depth, the distance from the document root down
 * to the list's own root. `margin-left` is a box-model property native list
 * rendering does not otherwise use, so this contribution is additive on top of
 * whatever positions the item within its own list — it moves the line box and
 * nothing inside it.
 *
 * What happens inside the line box is the list-grid section's business, and it
 * is not additive: those rules state `padding-inline-start` and `text-indent`
 * outright, replacing the pair Obsidian measures. The two are independent, which
 * is why they are separate rules — this one holds even with every rule below
 * removed.
 *
 * A list line reserves no gutter of its own — its native marker already
 * occupies one — so `--to-marker-gutter` does not appear in this calc. It IS
 * set on the line (`lineDecoration`), because the marker-column rules below
 * size the marker span to it and a fallback literal here would be a second copy
 * of `MARKER_GUTTER_CSS` to keep in step by hand. */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6 .cm-content > .cm-line.to-decor-list {
  margin-left: calc(var(--to-supp-depth, 0) * var(--to-decor-unit)) !important;
}

/*
 * LIST GEOMETRY (lists-on-the-outline-grid, docs/research/16). Everything here
 * hangs off `to-decor-list`, a class the decoration puts on LIST-ITEM LINES
 * ONLY, so both gates — outline mode, and "lists only" — come from the
 * decoration itself and these rules need no second condition. Outline mode off
 * is untouched: no class, none of this.
 *
 * The approach is to set the variables Obsidian's own list layout reads rather
 * than to fight the boxes it produces. Measured (research doc, E1/E3):
 * `--list-indent` drives `tab-size` on a list line and `min-width` on each
 * `.cm-indent` span, so pushing our own unit into it retargets every list level
 * at once — one indent step for every kind, which is the whole change.
 *
 * `rem`, not the `em`-based value Obsidian ships: `--list-indent` resolves
 * where it is USED, so an `em` unit inflates on a heading's larger font — the
 * Experiment 1 bug, reachable through a new door.
 *
 * What this does NOT get for free is the hanging indent; see `--to-list-hang`
 * below.
 */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6 .cm-content > .cm-line.to-decor-list {
  --list-indent: var(--to-decor-unit);

  /* Our own gradient draws every list level now (`computeLineGuides` publishes
   * their depths and `activeGuideDepths` folds them in), so Obsidian's own line
   * would double up on the same column. Only its BORDER goes: the `.cm-indent`
   * spans still do the layout, and they exist only while the user's own "Show
   * indentation guides" setting is on — which stays the user's to set. */
  --indentation-guide-width: 0px;
  --indentation-guide-width-active: 0px;

  /* A bullet is a marker like any other: same weight, same colour token, so a
   * snippet retunes lists and blocks together. 0.38em against Obsidian's 0.30em
   * default — measured against the block icons' ink, which are 0.85rem at
   * stroke-width 1.5 in this same `--text-faint`. */
  --list-bullet-size: 0.38em;
}

 * item's column, where every other kind centres its marker ON the column. That

 * it. Zeroing the gap and sizing the whole marker SPAN to the gutter is what

 * makes the text column font-independent: it is the gutter by construction,
 * rather than the sum of a padding, a glyph and a space.
 *
 * `min-width`, not `width`, so a wide ordered marker (`10. `) pushes its own
 * text out instead of overlapping it. That is the one place the text column is
 * not exactly the gutter, and it is deliberate: the alternative is a number
 * crossing into its own text.

 * because their marker is a `<label>` holding a real click target rather than a
 * span of glyphs — its width is the platform's, not this layer's to set. They
 * are not excluded from the COLUMN: the checkbox centres on it exactly as a
 * bullet does. An earlier version of this comment justified the exclusion as
 * "the checkbox is wider than the gutter", which was measured false — 16px
 * against 20px — and produced the misalignment real use reported.
 */

  .cm-content

  --list-padding-inline-start: 0px;

  /*
   * The hanging indent, STATED rather than read from Obsidian's own.
   *
   * `(depth − supplementalDepth)` is the item's depth within its own list, so
   * that many units is how far Obsidian's list rendering has already carried it
   * right of the line box; one gutter more is where its text begins. Wrapped
   * rows land exactly there.
   *
   * Obsidian computes this pair itself, from a live measurement, and gets it
   * wrong here twice over (both measured, research doc): the measurement takes
   * `coordsAtPos` at the end of the marker, which is the end of the marker's
   * TEXT rather than of its padded box, so with the span sized to the gutter
   * every wrapped row landed 16px left of its own item's text; and the value is
   * cached per line and invalidated only by a text change or a DOM mutation its
   * observer sees — `childList`, `characterData`, `subtree`, never attributes,
   * which is all a decoration changes — so turning outline mode on for an open
   * note left the old wrap column in place until a note switch.
   *
   * A stated value has neither problem, and needs no measurement of ours. The
   * `!important` is what beats Obsidian's own inline style; the same rule
   * `to-decor-block` already relies on.
   */
  --to-list-hang: calc(
    (var(--to-depth, 0) - var(--to-supp-depth, 0)) * var(--to-decor-unit) +
      var(--to-marker-gutter)
  );
  padding-inline-start: var(--to-list-hang) !important;
  text-indent: calc(-1 * var(--to-list-hang)) !important;
}

/*
 * The leading whitespace, sized to OUR depth instead of to what Obsidian made
 * of the characters.
 *
 * Obsidian wraps every list line's leading whitespace in one
 * `.cm-hmd-list-indent` span, and inside it quantises only what it recognises:
 * a tab or exactly four spaces becomes a `.cm-indent` of one `--list-indent`,
 * and whatever is left over stays a `.cm-indent-spacing` of literal space
 * glyphs. Measured, on a two-space-indented file: levels 1, 3 and 5 land on
 * columns and levels 2 and 4 land 8.38px right of the level above — the list
 * walks up the page at the font's space advance while our guides, drawn from
 * the parse, stay one unit apart. Every level is a level to the parse and to
 * reading mode; only the editor's whitespace arithmetic disagrees.
 *
 * Sizing the WRAPPER states the answer once, for whatever it contains: the
 * stated hang, less whatever the line's own marker occupies. That covers the
 * quantised part and the leftover together, so a two-space file, a three-space
 * file and a six-space level all land where the parse says they are.
 *
 * The subtraction is what keeps a CONTINUATION line right. A first line spends
 * the gutter on its native marker and its whitespace stops one gutter short of
 * its text; a continuation line has no marker and belongs under the item's
 * TEXT, so its whitespace takes the whole hang. Measured before this term
 * existed: a continuation landed on the marker's column, 20px left of the row
 * above it. Measured before this rule existed at all: 4.38px RIGHT of it under
 * a bullet and 8.56px right under `1. `, Obsidian sizing that span from the
 * whitespace rather than from the marker it is meant to sit under — the
 * long-standing misalignment `docs/research/12` records as unclosable without
 * exactly this override.
 *
 * It also removes this layer's dependence on the user's "Show indentation
 * guides" setting. Measured with it off: the `.cm-indent` spans are not emitted
 * at all, the wrapper holds raw text, and nothing is quantised — a FOUR-space
 * level then renders 7.25px left of its column. The wrapper is emitted either
 * way, so one rule covers both.
 *
 * `white-space: pre` and `overflow: hidden` keep whitespace wider than its own
 * box from wrapping the line or spilling over the marker; `vertical-align: top`
 * keeps an `overflow: hidden` inline-block — whose baseline would otherwise be
 * its bottom margin edge — from dropping the row it sits in.
 */
.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list
  .cm-hmd-list-indent {
  display: inline-block;
  width: calc(var(--to-list-hang) - var(--to-list-marker-cols, 0px));
  white-space: pre;
  overflow: hidden;
  vertical-align: top;
}

.markdown-source-view.mod-cm6
  .cm-content
  > .cm-line.to-decor-list:not(.HyperMD-task-line)
  .cm-formatting-list {
  display: inline-block;
  min-width: var(--to-marker-gutter);
}

/*
 * An ordered item's number is a node marker like any other, so it takes the
 * column too. It cannot CENTRE on it by shrinking its box the way a bullet does
 * — the glyphs ARE the mark, and their width is the font's and the number's —
 * so the box keeps its layout position (text stays at `column + gutter`) and
 * the painted glyphs are shifted left by a fixed amount. `transform` is what
 * makes that free: it moves the ink without moving anything around it. What the
 * shift buys is a shared LEFT EDGE, not centring; only a number narrow enough
 * to fit the gutter ends up centred, and that is a consequence rather than the
 * rule.
 *
 * The shift is a FIXED half-icon, not half the number's own width. Centring
 * each number on its own width was tried and measured: `1. ` centres exactly,
 * but `10. ` reaches 14px left of the column and `100. ` 19px, and nothing is
 * left for the fold chevron, which needs ~10px on that side and cannot go
 * further without crossing the parent level's guide. A fixed shift gives every
 * number in a list ONE left edge, which reads as a column rather than as ragged
 * centring, and leans wider ones right into their own text's space, which
 * `min-width` has already accounted for.
 *
 * Half the MARKER ICON, so that left edge is the block icon's left edge: a
 * number and a paragraph's icon at the same depth then start together, which
 * is the comparison a reader actually makes when a numbered list sits above a
 * paragraph. Half the gutter was tried first and put the digits 3.2px further
 * left than the icon beside them — measured, and visible.
 */

   * Obsidian's own trailing margin here is a second answer to the question the
   * gutter already answers — how far a mark's text sits from it.

   * from the marks it holds (chrome-tokens.ts), so it is free to land either
   * side of that threshold.

   * derivation can reach it.

}

/*

 * one space", which is the shortfall only when the marker's whitespace IS one
 * space; on `-  foo` or `-\tfoo` it was added on top of the whitespace already

 */

  .cm-content

  .list-bullet {

   * caret never sees it: on an item with content the position resolves to the
   * following content span and lands on the text column anyway, and on an empty
   * one the caret stops where the marker's glyphs stop.

Comments in committed code, workflows, and config must explain what is not visible from the code and will not expire. Three things must stay out: point-in-time data (timing tables, speedup ratios, observed flake rates, run counts, file counts, lists of which files currently do X), advocacy for the change being made, and restatements of the line below.

**Why:** Data-driven decisions are good; embedding the data in a comment is not. A benchmark table is true when written and silently wrong after the next runner image, dependency bump, or tuning pass, and a comment that has quietly become false is worse than no comment. Advocacy ("Measured, not picked", "earned its keep", "this is safe because I verified…") is writing aimed at a reviewer of the current PR, not a reader of the code a year on. See also [[docs-neutral-team-voice]].

**How to apply:** Before committing, reread every comment added and cut anything that (a) contains a number that could change, (b) names specific files/specs as an exhaustive list, (c) argues the change was correct, or (d) paraphrases the code.    * needs the file on disk can still wait for it, and a failed write still
   * reaches whoever asked for the toggle.

  toggle(path: string): { on: boolean; saved: Promise<void> } {
    const on = !this.paths.has(path);
    if (on) this.paths.add(path);
    else this.paths.delete(path);

  its own, so the decorations recompute only when `refreshDecorations` nudges the cursor — and
  `toggleMode` awaited `registry.toggle`, which awaited `saveData`, before reaching that nudge.

  a single `saveData` was measured at up to 754ms on a fast machine, against the ~500ms of
  fixed pauses the spec's `open()` spends before measuring. Reproduced exactly by slowing the
  write to 900ms: the first note came back with no `--to-depth` and the native marker column.

# outline-mode Specification

## Purpose
Defines outline mode: a per-note, UI-only toggle that gates access to structural editing
commands without ever modifying note content or metadata, persisted per file path in
plugin data across restarts and renames.
## Requirements
### Requirement: Per-note outline mode toggle
The plugin SHALL provide a command (and editor menu entry) that toggles outline mode for
the active markdown note. The mode SHALL be a pure editor-UI state: toggling it SHALL
never modify the note's content, metadata, or modification time.

#### Scenario: Toggling leaves the file untouched
- **WHEN** outline mode is toggled on and off for a note
- **THEN** the file's bytes and mtime are unchanged at every point

### Requirement: Mode persistence in plugin data
Outline mode state SHALL be remembered per note in the plugin data store (keyed by file
path), surviving app restarts. It SHALL never be written into the note (no frontmatter,
no markers). Renamed files SHALL keep their mode; deleted files SHALL be pruned from the
store.

#### Scenario: Mode survives restart
- **WHEN** outline mode is enabled for a note and Obsidian is restarted
- **THEN** the note reopens with outline mode enabled, and the note's content contains no
  trace of the mode

#### Scenario: Rename migrates state
- **WHEN** a note with outline mode enabled is renamed within Obsidian
- **THEN** the mode remains enabled under the new path

### Requirement: Mode gates structural commands
Structural editing commands SHALL be available only when the active note has outline mode
enabled (command palette `checkCallback` semantics), and the keyboard grammar SHALL
activate only for files with outline mode enabled. Notes without outline mode SHALL be
completely unaffected by the plugin's editing behavior: palette commands absent and every
grammar key binding declining, leaving stock editor behavior byte-for-byte.

#### Scenario: Commands inactive outside outline mode
- **WHEN** the command palette is opened for a note without outline mode
- **THEN** the structural commands are not offered for that note

#### Scenario: Keyboard grammar inactive outside outline mode
- **WHEN** any grammar-bound key (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Shift+Enter) is
  pressed in a note without outline mode

git commit -F - <<'MSG'
fix(mode): paint a mode toggle before the write that records it

`56-list-grid.e2e.ts`'s space-indent case failed intermittently on CI with a
depth-0 marker sitting ~15px right of its column. That number is not a geometry
error: it is where Obsidian's own native bullet sits on an UNDECORATED list
line, and the line carried no `--to-depth` at all, so the spec read `column` as
0 for a line whose real depth was 1. The whole note was rendering as a stock
note at the moment it was measured.

A mode toggle dispatches no CM6 transaction of its own, so the decorations
recompute only when `refreshDecorations` nudges the cursor — and `toggleMode`
awaited `registry.toggle`, which awaited `saveData`, before reaching that nudge.
Every visible consequence of a toggle therefore sat behind a `data.json` write.
Measured under load on a fast machine, a single `saveData` reached 754ms against
the ~500ms of fixed pauses the spec spends before measuring; reproduced exactly
by slowing the write to 900ms, which produced the CI state on the first note.
Two things kept it rare rather than deterministic: a pending toggle's
`nudgeFooters` dispatch lands on whatever note is open when the write finally
resolves, so a slow toggle silently repaints the NEXT note, and the failure
screenshot — captured a couple of round trips later — shows the note correctly
decorated.

`OutlineModeRegistry.toggle` now decides synchronously and hands back the write
still in flight. `toggleMode` flips the mode, raises the notice, nudges the
footers and repaints before its first yield, then awaits the write last so a
rejected write still surfaces where it did before. `forceRedraw` takes the same
shape: its off/on pair now happens within one turn instead of straddling two
writes, so a settings change no longer renders the note stock in between.

The new e2e case reads the DOM in the same synchronous turn as
`executeCommandById`, which no amount of waiting can make pass on the old code —
confirmed by reverting the fix. Full desktop suite green.

Docs: the diagnosis in docs/research/11, including that rAF is the wrong
instrument for this measurement (282-1890ms by rAF polling against 30-62ms by
MutationObserver, same run); the settings setters, which still have the old
shape, parked in docs/research/12.
